newsitem.title: GERMANY: Airbus plans to triple deliveries by 1999.
newsitem.headline: Airbus plans to triple deliveries by 1999.

text.p: European airplane consortium Airbus Industrie will triple its production over the next two years and have customers flying its planned "super jumbo" jet by 2003, the head of the group's German partner said in a newspaper interview.
Airbus also expected to reduce the job cuts it had planned to raise productivity and slash costs, Gustav Humbert, chief executive of Daimler-Benz Aerospace Airbus GmbH, told the Hamburg Abendblatt.
He said Airbus expected to produce 72 compact A319, A320 and A321 jetliners in 1996, about 130 in 1997, 173 in 1998 and 207 in 1999.
Airbus was also committed to producing the super jumbo A3XX now under development, even though rival Boeing Co has dropped its plan for s 300-seat plane"It will come whatever the case," Humbert said.

The production plans would bring investments of 280 million marks to the consortium's German plants, allowing far fewer job cuts than originally planned. "We have the the worst behind us," Humbert said.
